title: Cost-conscious generation of multiplexed short-read DNA libraries for whole-genome sequencing
author: Ashley Jones
materials: To measure a 96-well microplate of DNA samples with a dsDNA quantification high sensitivity kit (for microplate reader) (BioDynami or Thermo Fisher Scientific), ensure concentrations are ≤ 33 ng/µL. For instance, first quantify a few samples on a Qubit Fluorometer. Highly concentrated microplates of DNA can be diluted 1/10 before starting (e.g. 5 µL of DNA added to 45 µL nuclease-free water in a new 96-well microplate). dsDNA quantification high sensitivity kits have a quantification range of 0.2 to 100 ng. This protocol will quantify 3 µL of DNA at a concentration of ≤ 33 ng/µL. Highly concentrated samples are difficult to measure on microplate readers. Reducing gain on fluorescent microplate reader to 80% can help but will be at the cost of accuracy.
Proceed to pooling or store at -20°C.

Quantify the DNA libraries as previously described, using a dsDNA quantification high sensitivity kit for microplate reader (BioDynami or Thermo Fisher Scientific), or a Qubit Fluorometer for low-throughput samples. Optional, but this helps provide a more uniform pooling of samples. Pooling samples based on concentration asssumes samples have a similar average insert size; true molarity may vary. To measure molarity, use a high sensitive automated electrophoresis system, such as LabChip GX devices (PerkinElmer) or Bioanalyzer/TapeStation devices (Agilent Technologies).

Prior to PippinHT size selection, the library may need to be concentrated, which can be done with AMPure XP beads (or equivalent) according to the manufacturer's inctructions (Beckman Coulter). Alternatively, to concentrate large pools of library, use a MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen 28004), according to the manufacturer's inctructions.

Quantify the DNA samples. For a low-throughput number of samples, quantify with a Qubit Fluorometer according to the manufacturer's instructions (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The following describes quantification in high-throughput (96-well microplates) by reading on a fluorescent microplate reader.

steps.title: Prepare quantification working solution
steps.instruction: Mix dsDNA HS dye/reagent with dsDNA buffer at a 1:200 ratio to make a working solution; each reaction will use 97 µL of this solution plus 3 µL DNA (total 100 µL). For a full 96‑well plate (96 samples, 32 standards, 22 µL dead volume) prepare 14 477 µL dsDNA buffer and 73 µL dsDNA HS reagent (for 1 plate) or 28 954 µL buffer and 146 µL reagent (for 2 plates). Manual multi‑channel pipetting can reduce dead volume to ≈12 samples per plate; automated JANUS workstations require ≥1 mL dead volume.

steps.title: Allocate quantification solution to plates
steps.instruction: Transfer 97 µL of the quantification working solution into the first two columns of each 96‑well microplate (16 wells per plate) to serve as duplicate standards.

steps.title: Add DNA samples to sample wells
steps.instruction: Add 3 µL of each DNA sample to the designated sample columns of the microplates.

steps.title: Add standards to standard wells
steps.instruction: Add 3 µL of each standard to the standard columns in duplicate, using the concentration series 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 ng/µL, then repeat the series in the next column.

steps.title: Seal, vortex and incubate plates
steps.instruction: Seal each microplate with adhesive film, vortex briefly, spin down, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min protected from light. Fluorescence remains stable for ~3 h.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence on plate reader
steps.instruction: Read fluorescence on a microplate reader using ~480 nm excitation / ~530 nm emission (or kit‑specific maxima: 495/540 nm high‑sensitivity, 485/545 nm broad‑range, 502/523 µM high‑sensitivity, 510/527 µM broad‑range). For FLUOstar Omega set gain to 80 %; for Tecan Infinite M1000 PRO use 5 nm bandwidth, top mode, 100 Hz × 10 flashes, Z‑position 20 000 µm, gain ~96 % (adjust lower if signals are high). Ensure whole‑plate read and correct plate settings.

steps.title: Generate standard curve
steps.instruction: Plot standard concentrations versus fluorescence, fit a straight line, and calculate DNA concentrations of all samples using the curve. Example calculation files are provided in the supplemental material.

steps.title: Dilute DNA samples to 1‑2 ng/µL
steps.instruction: Dilute each DNA sample to a final concentration of 1‑2 ng/µL (≈1.5 ng/µL) in ~25 µL total volume. Transfer nuclease‑free water to a new 96‑well PCR plate, then add the calculated volume of DNA. For JANUS workstations use 25 µL tips (larger volumes may be needed for highly concentrated samples).

steps.title: Mix diluted samples
steps.instruction: Mix each well thoroughly, briefly spin down if needed, seal with adhesive film and store at –20 °C until tagmentation.

steps.title: Optional re‑quantify and re‑dilute
steps.instruction: If necessary, repeat the quantification and dilution steps as described above. The Illumina Bead‑Linked Transposome (BLT) can tolerate a wide concentration range, reducing the need for further dilution.

steps.title: Prepare tagmentation master mix
steps.instruction: For 102 reactions (96 samples + 6 dead volume) combine per reaction: 3 µL 2× TMP (custom buffer), 0.2 µL BLT, 2.8 µL DNA (1‑2 ng/µL). Total master mix volume = 326.4 µL (3.2 µL per reaction). Aliquot 3.2 µL into each well of a 384‑well plate (or 96‑well plate if preferred). This uses 1/50th the BLT volume of standard Illumina protocols.

steps.title: Pre‑heat heat block to 53 °C
steps.instruction: Set a PCR machine or heat block to 53 °C (suitable for a 384‑well plate) and allow it to equilibrate before use.

steps.title: Dispense tagmentation mix into plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 3.2 µL of the tagmentation master mix into each of the 96 wells of the first quadrant of the 384‑well plate (or equivalent wells of a 96‑well plate). Leftover master mix can be stored at 4 °C for limited time.

steps.title: Add DNA to tagmentation wells
steps.instruction: Add 2.8 µL of each diluted DNA sample (1‑2 ng/µL) to the corresponding well containing master mix and pipette‑mix gently.

steps.title: Seal and incubate tagmentation
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with PCR‑grade adhesive film, vortex lightly (keep liquid at the bottom), and incubate at 53 °C for 30 min with shaking at 300‑450 rpm (or vortex at 15 min intervals if no shaker). No stop solution or cleanup is required.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: For 102 reactions (96 samples + 6 dead volume) combine per reaction: 28.15 µL nuclease‑free water, 7.5 µL 5× Q5 reaction buffer, 1 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 0.35 µL Q5 High‑Fidelity DNA Polymerase, 4 µL 2.5 µM i5 index primer, 4 µL 2.5 µM i7 index primer, 5 µL tagmentation product (added later). Total master mix = 50 µL; aliquot 37 µL per well of a 96‑well PCR plate. (If using JANUS G3, prepare for 28 samples ×4 tubes as indicated.)

steps.title: Dispense PCR master mix to plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 37 µL of the PCR master mix into each well of a fresh 96‑well PCR plate.

steps.title: Add dual index primers
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL of a 2.5 µM i5 index primer and 4 µL of a 2.5 µM i7 index primer to each well, ensuring a unique i5‑i7 combination per sample (8 i5 primers across rows, 12 i7 primers down columns). Label tubes and plate orientation carefully; automation is recommended to avoid errors.

steps.title: Add tagmentation template
steps.instruction: Transfer 5 µL of the completed tagmentation reaction from the 384‑well plate into each corresponding well of the PCR plate containing the master mix and primers.

steps.title: Seal and vortex PCR plate
steps.instruction: Seal the PCR plate with PCR‑grade adhesive film, vortex briefly, and centrifuge just enough to collect liquid at the bottom (avoid pelleting beads).

steps.title: Run PCR program
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler: 72 °C 3 min; 98 °C 3 min; 12‑16 cycles of 98 °C 45 s, 62 °C 30 s, 72 °C 2 min; final extension 72 °C 1 min; hold ≤10 °C. Use 16 cycles as a default but fewer cycles can reduce duplicate fragments.

steps.title: Resuspend and separate BLT beads (if used)
steps.instruction: Flick‑mix and briefly vortex the BLT bead tube to resuspend, place on a magnetic rack for 5 min (or until beads pellet), then transfer the supernatant to a new tube, discarding beads. Keep a 10 µL aliquot for QC if desired.

steps.title: Pool libraries into single tube
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL nuclease‑free water to a 1.5 mL tube, then transfer an equal volume (e.g., 10 µL) from each of the 96 libraries into the tube (total ≈1 mL). This step can be automated with a CSV volume file.

steps.title: Perform size selection on PippinHT
steps.instruction: Load the pooled library onto a Sage Science PippinHT using a 2 % agarose cassette. Select a size range of 430‑600 bp (ideal for Illumina 150 bp PE). Load 20 µL DNA + 5 µL marker per lane (max 1.5 µg, up to 3 µg tolerated). Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for automatic selection and gel purification.

steps.title: Clean library with AMPure XP beads
steps.instruction: Purify the size‑selected pool using AMPure XP (or equivalent) beads at 0.5‑1× the pool volume according to the bead‑manufacturer’s protocol. Beads supplied with the Illumina DNA Prep kit may be reused after adjusting for volume.

steps.title: Optional second AMPure cleanup
steps.instruction: If short fragments or primers remain, perform a second AMPure XP cleanup at 0.6× the volume.

steps.title: Quality‑check final library
steps.instruction: Analyze the final library on a high‑sensitivity electrophoresis system (LabChip GX, Agilent Bioanalyzer or TapeStation). Include an aliquot of the un‑cleaned pool for comparison. Expected size for NovaSeq 150 bp PE is 400‑600 bp; double peaks indicate over‑amplification, and very large peaks (>1 kb) suggest insufficient tagmentation.

steps.title: Quantify library with Qubit
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration at least twice using a Qubit Fluorometer with the dsDNA High‑Sensitivity assay kit; calculate the average concentration.

steps.title: Calculate library molarity
steps.instruction: Compute molarity (nM) using: nM = (ng/µL × 10⁶) / (660 g·mol⁻¹ × average fragment size in bp). Use the average fragment length from the QC electrophoresis.

steps.title: Dilute library for sequencing
steps.instruction: Dilute the library to the sequencing provider’s required concentration (typically 2‑10 nM) with nuclease‑free water, then store at –20 °C until shipment.

steps.title: Ship library on ice
steps.instruction: Package the library on ice, using cold packs or dry ice as needed, and send to the sequencing facility (e.g., Illumina NovaSeq 6000, 300‑cycle flowcell for 150 bp paired‑end reads).
